Expected Result
HTTP 200; all four top-level fields present/non-null; every segmentRefId in seatMapDetails also appears in flightSegments
Actual Result

TC-BOOK-POS-04 - Verify a selected seat is committed to the booking as soon as Book succeeds, without waiting on any ticketing/payment stepPASS
Endpoint Name: Check that a chosen seat is already locked into the booking the moment it's confirmed, without waiting for a separate ticketing step
Request: Booked a flight with a seat chosen, then immediately looked the booking back up
Response: The seat was already fully attached and priced in that very first lookup
Expected: The seat shouldn't need a separate later step to be committed to the booking
Actual: Confirmed - this airline issues tickets immediately, so there's no separate window to isolate, but the core assertion holds
Status: PASS
Evidence

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier GulfAir, CredentialsSelector KSA, environment staging (ne-3).
Steps
  1. 4 variants of a no-seat Book payload, each on a fresh offer: omit ResponseId (chain L), omit selectedOfferId/supplier/credentialsSelector (chain M)
Expected Result
All four runs rejected; no pnr created in any run
Actual Result
3 of 4 sub-cases correctly rejected with clean 400s (consistent with BUG-13 remaining RESOLVED - no 500s observed). The ResponseId-omission sub-case is STILL open (still creates a real ticketed PNR when omitted, unchanged since Round 1) - excluded from this test case's own tally per the established scope convention, but explicitly flagged here rather than silently dropped.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected (or returns an explicit not-supported response) when called for an offer whose isSeatMapRequired flag was falseFAIL
Endpoint Name: Check that the seat map feature refuses to run for a flight that was already flagged as not needing a seat map
Request: Looked up the seat map anyway, for an offer this airline itself had already flagged as not requiring one
Response: It returned a full seat map anyway, with no warning that this wasn't supposed to be offered
Expected: Should be refused or flagged, since the flight itself says a seat map isn't needed
Actual: Not caught - the seat map feature ignores this airline's own earlier flag and returns full data regardless
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Same GetSeatMap call as TC-SEATMAP-POS-01; isSeatMapRequired=false confirmed at FareConfirm on all chains

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier GulfAir, CredentialsSelector KSA, environment staging (ne-3).
Steps
  1. POST api/V2/SeatMap/Seat using AddPassenger IDs from an offer confirmed live (isSeatMapRequired=false) - reconfirmed on 17 independent chains this round
Expected Result
Rejected or an explicit unsupported-operation envelope
Actual Result
Still 200 with a fully populated seatMapDetails on every one of 17 chains this round on ne-3. STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-15, 2nd consecutive round it has been separately numbered; identical since Round 1).
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected when the request otherwise targets a valid offer but no segment of that offer's itinerary is being queried (cross-offer ResponseId/selectedOfferId)FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check that a seat map lookup is refused when its two reference numbers come from two completely different flight bookings
Request: Mixed reference numbers from two unrelated bookings and looked up the seat map both ways
Response: Both attempts returned a full seat map with no complaint about the mismatch
Expected: Should be refused, since the two reference numbers don't belong together
Actual: Not caught in either direction - a full seat map was returned regardless
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Cross A->B and B->A GetSeatMap calls both returned 200 with populated seatMapDetails

Preconditions
Supplier GulfAir, CredentialsSelector KSA, environment staging (ne-3).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap called with ResponseId from Chain A's AddPassenger (BAH-RUH) but selectedOfferId from Chain B's AddPassenger (BAH-JED, unrelated), and the reverse direction
Expected Result
Rejected
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-01, 6th consecutive round including this ne-3 run) - accepted with HTTP 200 in both directions
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-03 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects a stale or entirely invalid ResponseId/selectedOfferId pairPASS
Endpoint Name: Check that the seat map feature refuses a completely made-up reference number, and see what happens with a real but already-used one
Request: Tried a fabricated reference number, then a real reference number from a booking that had already been completed
Response: The fabricated reference was correctly refused with a clear error; the already-used real reference still worked and returned a seat map
Expected: The fabricated one should be refused; the already-used one is a separate, previously-unclear question
Actual: Fabricated reference correctly refused; a real reference keeps working even after the booking it belongs to is finished
Status: PASS
Evidence
Run 1 TransactionId 97a134aa-a38e-4db8-8484-c36582abf45d (400); Run 2: Chain A's already-used AddPassenger IDs still return 200

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier GulfAir, CredentialsSelector KSA, environment staging (ne-3).
Steps
  1. Run 1: fabricated GUID ResponseId + fabricated selectedOfferId string. Run 2: genuine but already-consumed AddPassenger ID pair (Chain A, already Booked)
Expected Result
Rejected; no seatMapDetails returned for either
Actual Result
A genuinely fabricated pair is cleanly rejected with 400 ValidationError. Confirmed again: a real but already-consumed pair is NOT rejected (200) - IDs are not invalidated after being consumed.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects requests with each mandatory field individually omitted: supplier, credentialsSelector, ResponseId, selectedOfferIdFAIL
Endpoint Name: Check that a seat map lookup is refused whenever any one of its four required fields is missing
Request: Ran four variations, each missing exactly one required field
Response: Three of the four were correctly refused; the fourth (a missing booking-session reference) still returned a full seat map
Expected: All four should be refused
Actual: Three fixed, one still open - omitting that one particular field still silently succeeds
Status: FAIL
Evidence
omit supplier 400; omit credentialsSelector 400; omit selectedOfferId 400; omit ResponseId 200 (full seatMapDetails returned)
Attempt 1 of 4 - omit supplier

Request: Booked a 2-passenger Jeddah flight, but attached a seat ID that actually came from an unrelated Riyadh flight's seat map
Response: The booking succeeded and tickets were issued, but the seat selection silently disappeared from the confirmation - no seat was actually attached, and no error was shown
Expected: The system should refuse the booking, since the seat ID doesn't belong to this flight
Actual: Still not caught - the booking goes through as if no seat had ever been requested, with no warning to the caller that their seat choice was dropped
Status: FAIL
Evidence
pnr TVJNGU, passengersSelectedSeats:{}, totalSelectedSeatsAmount:null

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier GulfAir, CredentialsSelector KSA, environment staging (ne-3).
Steps
  1. Book using Chain B's (2-ADT, BAH-JED) ResponseId/selectedOfferId, but passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1.cellId taken from Chain A's (BAH-RUH) GetSeatMap response, cellCode=Chain B's own valid code (8A)
Expected Result
Request rejected (400 ValidationError) since cellId appears to embed offer-bound metadata
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-07, 6th consecutive round including this ne-3 run) - accepted with no error at all; booking created and ticketed with the seat selection silently vanished
TC-BOOK-VAL-06 - Validate Book's behavior when passengersSelectedSeats.cellCode does not match the cell that cellId actually encodesFAIL
Endpoint Name: Check what happens when a seat's visible label and its internal ID code point to two different seats
Request: Submitted a booking where the visible seat label said one seat, but the seat's internal ID code actually belonged to a different seat
Response: The system booked and charged for the seat matching the visible label, ignoring what the internal ID code actually pointed to
Expected: Clarify whether the visible label or the internal ID is authoritative when the two disagree
Actual: The visible label wins - the internal ID code appears to be decorative and isn't independently checked
Status: FAIL
Evidence
pnr TCKQJQ, cellCode 8B booked at 120.00 SAR (8B's own price, cellId was for cell 8A)

[BUG-01, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] GetSeatMap accepts a ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair sourced from two unrelated offers (both directions) and returns a fully populated seatMapDetails instead of rejecting the mismatched identifiers. (TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02)

Expected value: 400 ValidationError rejecting the cross-offer identifier pair

Defect
[BUG-02, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] GetSeatMap succeeds (200) even when ResponseId is omitted entirely from an otherwise-valid request. (TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04)
Field: ResponseId (GetSeatMap request, omitted)
Expected value: 400 ValidationError: 'The ResponseId field is required.'
Impact: Mandatory-field validation is inconsistently enforced - selectedOfferId/supplier/credentialsSelector omission is correctly rejected but ResponseId omission is not, an asymmetric validation gap.
Defect
[BUG-03, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] SeatAfterHold rejects every call for supplier=GulfAir with HTTP 409 'GulfAir does not exists', reconfirmed against a brand-new fresh Hold (pnr TYOBGG). (TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-POS-01)
Field: supplier (SeatAfterHold request)
Expected value: 200 with a seat-selection response, or a documented, GulfAir-specific not-supported response distinct from this generic-looking supplier-existence error
Impact: SeatAfterHold is entirely unusable for GulfAir's Hold branch - no seat can ever be attached to a GulfAir Hold-then-finalize booking.
Defect
[BUG-04, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] Hold's holdExpirationDate is still null for GulfAir, reconfirmed on 3 fresh Holds this round (TYOBGG, TXMQCN, TQZRGI). (TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-02)
Field: holdExpirationDate (Hold response)
Expected value: 2026-09-06T[some future time]Z (a real ISO-8601 datetime the number of minutes/hours ahead per the supplier's hold-TTL policy)
Impact: Downstream cannot compute the Family-B hold's expiry, so cleanup/expiry tracking can't run and expired-hold negative tests (TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-NEG-02) can't be forced deterministically.
Defect
[BUG-06, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] Book does not decode or verify the cellId token at all - a tampered cellId (last 10 base64 chars replaced) is accepted and the seat is attached purely based on the submitted cellCode (pnr TRIBZV). (TC-BOOK-NEG-06)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<pax>.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>.cellId (Book request)
Expected value: 400 ValidationError rejecting the tampered/unverifiable cellId token
Impact: cellId's apparent role as a signed/metadata-bearing token is not actually enforced server-side - any syntactically-similar string attached to a valid cellCode will be accepted, undermining the token's integrity purpose.
Defect
[BUG-07, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] Book silently drops a cross-offer cellId's seat selection instead of rejecting the request (pnr TVJNGU, passengersSelectedSeats:{}). (TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats (Book response, cross-offer cellId)
Expected value: 400 ValidationError rejecting the cross-offer cellId, OR an explicit acknowledgement in the response that the seat selection was dropped
Impact: The caller believes a seat was requested but the booking silently proceeds without it and without any seat fee charged - a silent-failure UX/billing-integrity gap, not a hard rejection.
Defect
[BUG-08, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] Hold silently accepts and honors an undocumented passengersSelectedSeats field for GulfAir (pnr TQZRGI, confirmed on a fresh never-Held offer). (FLOW-V2-50-SEATFIELD)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats (Hold request/response)
Expected value: The field should be rejected (schema validation error) or explicitly ignored per SPEC.md §2.10's documented Hold contract, which does not list this field
Impact: Contradicts SPEC.md §1.10 item 6's asymmetry finding that Hold has no seat-selection mechanism and SeatAfterHold exists specifically to fill that gap - if Hold already accepts seats directly, SeatAfterHold's entire purpose is undermined/redundant.
Defect
[BUG-09, STILL REPRODUCES IN ITS WORSENED FORM on ne-3] A Child passenger can be booked and ticketed into an exit-row seat with zero server-side validation (pnr TXYGDL). (TC-BOOK-BIZ-05)
Field: passengersSelectedSeats.<CHD paxRef> (Book request, exit-row cell)
Expected value: An error response (candidate RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD) with no pnr created
Impact: A real safety-regulation violation (exit-row seating has hard age/capability requirements under aviation regulation) can be booked and ticketed through the API with no server-side gate at all.
Defect
[BUG-10, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] AddPassenger rejects a passengersList/travelDocument name mismatch (e.g. middle name 'kady' vs '') with HTTP 400 'Invalid travel document information', identical to prior rounds. Confirmed via a targeted probe this round (chain O) after noting the collection's own current saved example actually carries matching middle names on both sides and succeeds cleanly - the mismatch-rejection behavior is real and reproducible, just not triggered by the collection's unmodified saved example as currently worded. (TC-BOOK-NEG-12)
Field: passengersList.<pax>.name.middle / travelDocument.name.middle (AddPassenger request, PRE-FLIGHT probe)
Expected value: UNKNOWN whether an exact-match requirement between passengersList.name and travelDocument.name is an intentional business rule (real passports can legitimately have formatting differences from booking-entry names) or an overly strict validation - SPEC.md §2.5 does not document this as a hard requirement either way
Impact: If unintentional, this could reject legitimate real-world passengers whose booking name entry doesn't byte-for-byte match their travel document (common for middle names/suffixes) - a false-negative risk for real bookings.
Defect
[BUG-11, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] Resubmitting an already-consumed Book request returns HTTP 409 with OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse present in the error body, containing a live supplier apiKey/secretKey in plaintext inside the embedded SOAP envelope. Confirmed via direct Book resubmission this round (in addition to Hold's 609-conflict path noted in Round 5) - the leak spans at least the Book and Hold conflict paths. (TC-BOOK-POS-03)
Field: OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse (error envelope, 609 duplicate-booking conflict)
Expected value: The error envelope should omit OriginalSupplierRequest/OriginalSupplierResponse entirely, or redact the embedded <apiKey>/<secretKey> elements before returning them to the caller
Impact: A caller who resubmits a duplicate Book/Hold request receives live, plaintext third-party (supplier) credentials in the error response - a credential-exposure security defect, not merely a verbose-error annoyance.
Defect
[BUG-15, STILL REPRODUCES on ne-3] GetSeatMap does not reject or flag a call made against an offer whose isSeatMapRequired capability flag is false at FareConfirm time - it still returns HTTP 200 with a fully populated seatMapDetails. (TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01)
Field: seatMapDetails (GetSeatMap response, isSeatMapRequired=false offer)
Expected value: A 409 OperationNotSupported envelope (matching GetOfferBundles's confirmed pattern for haveBundles=false offers), or at minimum an explicit flag in the response
Impact: Callers cannot trust isSeatMapRequired=false as a reliable signal to skip GetSeatMap - the endpoint will happily return a seat map anyway, undermining the capability-flag contract described in SPEC.md §2.2.
